newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk court cancels part of unamended sell-off law.
newsitem.headline: Turk court cancels part of unamended sell-off law.

text.p: The Turkish constitutional court on Wednesday cancelled part of the privatisation law after an objection filed by opposition MPs, the court's chief judge said.
"It has been cancelled with a majority of votes," Judge Yekta Gungor Ozden told reporters.
The cancellation will not in practical terms have an adverse effect on Turkey's privatisation process as parliament earlier ratified an amendment to the articles cancelled by the court.
The law amendment was related to the evaluation of companies slated for privatisation and to the format of sell-off tenders, according to the Official Gazette.

The amendment also allows the deputy prime minister to be part of the High Board of Privatisation, the top decision making body in state sell-offs, chaired by the prime minister and including five senior cabinet ministers.

The request to annul the amended articles was lodged at the constitutional court last year by opposition MPs, who said the procedure for the creation of evaluation committees was against the constitution.
